Title: Research through Design (RtD)
Description: Explored generative design spaces and tangible user interactions through physical prototyping and research-through-design methodology within the MSc IPD curriculum.
Tags: Design Research;Research through Design;Interaction Design;Physical Prototyping;Concept Development
longDescription: During my MSc in Integrated Product Design at TU Delft, I explored research through design as a way to investigate how people interact with physical objects. The work combined open-ended design exploration with tangible prototyping: making something was not only a way to present a concept, but also a way to ask questions and learn from the interaction itself. This approach helped connect research, experimentation and product development. Rather than focusing only on a finished object, the project placed value on the process of exploring and refining possible design directions.

Title: Klimmende Stapelaar
Description: Engineered and prototyped a climbing stacker mechanism during the Mechanical Engineering BSc at TU Delft, focusing on kinematics, stress analysis, and functional validation.
longDescription: This Mechanical Engineering bachelor's project centred on a climbing stacker mechanism. The challenge was to translate a desired movement into a workable mechanical design, and then see how the concept behaved as a physical prototype. The project combined kinematic reasoning, stress analysis and mechanical design with building and functional testing. It is an example of the engineering work I enjoy most: making design choices based on calculations, translating them into parts and assemblies, and checking whether the resulting mechanism actually performs as intended.

Title: Custom Mini Vehicle
Description: Designed and fabricated a miniature vehicle prototype from scratch, engineering the custom chassis, gearing ratio, and steering assembly for stability and efficiency.
longDescription: I designed and fabricated a small vehicle prototype, starting with the mechanical layout rather than a ready-made chassis. The work included the custom frame, drivetrain gearing and steering assembly. An important part of the challenge was getting these elements to function together within the limited space of a miniature vehicle, while considering stability and efficient motion. It was a hands-on project in which component design, fabrication and assembly were closely connected. The result was a physical vehicle prototype and an opportunity to apply mechanical engineering principles to an integrated product.

Title: Direct Air Carbon Capture Paper
Description: Conducted a research study and thermodynamic feasibility analysis on a mechanical Direct Air Capture (DAC) machine for carbon mitigation, modeling scalability and energy demands.
Tags: Engineering Research;Thermodynamics;Energy Analysis;Feasibility Analysis;Carbon Capture;Technical Writing
longDescription: This research project investigated direct air capture (DAC) from a mechanical and thermodynamic perspective. I studied the feasibility of a machine that removes carbon dioxide directly from ambient air, with particular attention to its energy demand and the implications of scaling the system. The work was analytical rather than a physical design-and-build project. Its value for my portfolio is in the engineering reasoning: taking a broad environmental challenge, breaking it down into relevant physical processes and using a thermodynamic assessment to understand the limitations of a proposed solution.

Title: Mini CNC Machine
Description: Designed and assembled a functional 3-axis desktop CNC machine, integrating precision linear rails, stepper motor motion control, and custom structural brackets.
longDescription: I designed and assembled a compact three-axis CNC machine, bringing together a structural frame, precision linear guides, stepper-motor-driven motion and custom brackets. The project required the mechanical layout and motion system to be considered together: the machine needed a clear path for each axis, properly supported components and an assembly that could actually be built. The finished prototype demonstrates how mechanical design and basic mechatronics meet in practice. For my portfolio, this project is particularly useful because the process and result can be shown through CAD, assembly details and photographs of the machine itself.

Title: Baxter Roll
Description: Developed a considered product concept through research, mechanical development, prototyping, and iteration with a focus on how the final experience should feel to use.
Tags: Product Design;Design Research;Mechanical Design;Concept Development;Physical Prototyping;Design Iteration
longDescription: Baxter Roll was a product design and engineering project that combined research, mechanical development and physical prototyping. The aim was not just to reach a mechanically workable concept, but to consider the experience of using the product as the design evolved. The process involved moving between research, concept development and iterations of the prototype, with attention to how design decisions affected both function and interaction. This is the type of work that connects my background in mechanical engineering to Integrated Product Design.

Title: Hyperion Lyceum
Description: Completed pre-university education (VWO) at Hyperion Lyceum in Amsterdam with a strong focus on mathematics, natural sciences, and analytical philosophy as preparation for TU Delft.
longDescription: Before starting at TU Delft, I completed VWO at Hyperion Lyceum in Amsterdam. Mathematics and the natural sciences formed an important part of that foundation, alongside subjects that encouraged analytical thinking and reflection. This background led into my Mechanical Engineering studies and later my interest in product design.

Title: IDE Business Fair
Short description: Chair, IDE Business Fair organising committee
Description: Chaired the organising committee of the TU Delft IDE Business Fair (17–18 March 2026), bringing design students and companies together. I helped recruit participating companies and coordinated outreach around internships, graduation projects, careers and event activities.
Tags: Leadership;Event Organization;Company Acquisition;Project Management;Stakeholder Communication;Company Relations
longDescription:
As chair of the organising committee for the IDE Business Fair at TU Delft, I helped organise the 17–18 March 2026 edition of an event connecting Industrial Design Engineering students with companies. The fair provides opportunities for students to explore internships, graduation projects and first jobs, while giving companies a chance to meet future designers and engineers.

My role included coordinating the committee and approaching potential participating companies. I was involved in company recruitment and outreach, explaining the value of the event and discussing possible formats such as exhibition stands, workshops, design cases and other interactions with students. This meant combining practical event organisation with external communication and working towards the needs of both companies and students.

Alongside my design and engineering work, the project reflects my interest in taking responsibility, organising people and building relationships between different stakeholders. The experience gave me a broader view of how design-oriented companies connect with students and what they look for in future colleagues.

Title: Offshore Workability Analysis
Short description: Feasibility studies for offshore access operations.
Description: Analyse weather data, vessel specifications, and operational limits at Ampelmann to assess whether planned motion-compensated walk-to-work operations are viable before they go to sea.
Tags: Offshore;AutoCAD;VS Code;GitHub;Organization;Workability Analysis;Wave Data Analysis;Technical Reporting
longDescription: At Ampelmann, I work on offshore workability analysis for motion-compensated walk-to-work operations. The central question is whether a planned transfer operation is feasible within the expected environmental and operational limits. This means bringing together weather and wave data, vessel information and relevant equipment constraints to support decisions before operations take place offshore. The work also involves technical reporting and working with engineering information and digital tools. Unlike a physical product-design project, this experience shows how I handle real operational constraints, assess technical feasibility and communicate engineering conclusions in a professional setting.

Title: High School STEM Tutoring
Description: Provided 1-on-1 tutoring and exam preparation for secondary school students in mathematics, physics, and chemistry (wiskunde & natuurkunde), translating complex concepts into intuitive methods.
longDescription: As a tutor, I helped secondary-school students prepare for mathematics, physics and chemistry courses and examinations. The work was largely one-to-one, so I had to find explanations that suited each student's understanding rather than repeat a fixed lesson. A large part of tutoring technical subjects is identifying where a problem becomes confusing and breaking it into manageable steps. Although it is different from designing a physical product, it has been useful practice in explaining technical ideas clearly, listening carefully and adapting communication to the person in front of me.

Title: Platenmeubel (Vinyl Cabinet)
Description: Designed and hand-crafted a bespoke wooden cabinet tailored for vinyl records and turntable setup, prioritizing clean joinery, acoustic decoupling, and warmth.
longDescription: I designed and built a wooden cabinet around my turntable and vinyl collection. The aim was to create a piece of furniture that worked as practical record storage while fitting the visual character of a listening setup. The design combines an upper surface for the record player with space for storing records, finished in warm-toned wood. The cabinet also uses ribbed panels and warm lighting as visible design features. I approached it as both a hands-on woodworking project and a small product-design exercise, balancing the proportions, material appearance, functionality and details of the finished piece.

Title: Ergonomic Laptop Stand
Description: Designed and fabricated an elevated laptop stand focused on ergonomic posture, passive thermal airflow, and clean tactile aesthetics for everyday desk use.
longDescription: I designed and made a laptop stand intended to improve the everyday experience of working at a desk. The concept lifts the screen to a more comfortable viewing position while leaving space for passive airflow around the laptop. In addition to these practical requirements, I paid attention to the product's shape and tactile appearance so that it would feel at home in a simple workspace. This small personal project demonstrates how even a straightforward object benefits from considering ergonomics, physical construction and visual design together.

Title: Photography
Short description: Stills shaped by light, texture, and overlooked moments.
Description: Photographing with whatever is to hand and looking for the in-between moments that do not ask to be noticed. The work is led by atmosphere, composition, and natural light.
longDescription: Photography is a personal practice in looking closely at everyday surroundings. I am drawn to natural light, material textures, composition and moments that might otherwise pass unnoticed. I tend to work with whichever camera is available and focus more on atmosphere than on producing heavily staged images. Although photography is not an engineering project, it informs how I observe objects and spaces, frame details and communicate ideas visually. I include it in my portfolio as a complementary creative interest rather than as a technical design case study.

Title: Writing & Production
Short description: Instrumental music focused on texture and space.
Description: Writing and producing mostly instrumental music with an interest in texture, space, and ideas that take a moment to resolve.
longDescription: I write and produce mostly instrumental music, with a particular interest in texture, space and the way an idea develops over time. I enjoy experimenting with how different sounds relate to one another and how relatively small changes in arrangement can change the feeling of a track. This work is separate from my formal engineering studies, but it reflects a similar interest in experimentation, iteration and attention to detail. In my portfolio it provides a view of my creative work outside physical product design.

Title: EasyTabMaker
Description: When I could not find a free guitar tab maker which felt intuitive to use and had no intrucive ads. I decided to make my own, easytabmaker.com has a simple interface and tabs can be shared and accesed though accounts.
longDescription: I started EasyTabMaker because I could not find a free guitar-tab editor that felt straightforward to use and did not rely on intrusive advertising. Instead of adapting to an interface I disliked, I decided to create my own. The result is a web application centred on a simple way to write guitar tabs, with accounts that allow tabs to be accessed and shared. The project connects two of my interests: music and making useful tools. It also gave me a practical opportunity to think about interaction design from the perspective of someone who would actually use the product. The current version can be found at easytabmaker.com.
